summary: Cox Point Light: a red-and-white skeleton tower on Grand Lake, New Brunswick, lit in the early 1870s and kept by the Cox family, then Alexander McBaine, for decades.

lens.note: Seventh-order lens and lamp replaced the reflectors in 1905 (Marine report 1904-05; LighthouseFriends). Current optic not given.

structures.note: Earlier square wooden tower. Lighthouse Digest gives 1869 as its build year; the sources disagree on the first light's date.

Reinforced concrete tower built at a cost of $985 during McBaine's service (LighthouseFriends); replaced the earlier wooden tower (Lighthouse Digest). Lighthouse Directory photo caption: second (1917) lighthouse.

Triangular skeleton tower with red and white rectangular daymark (CCG). Height 3.5 m (11 ft) per LighthouseFriends and the Fredericton Capital Region; CCG list gives 3.6 m (structure height, list 141); Lighthouse Directory gives 7.5 m (25 ft) on a square pyramidal concrete base. Material not stated in sources; steel is not given and is omitted.

access.note: Reached by road. Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Directory).

events.note: LighthouseFriends narrative: operation began 3 May 1871. Its data table and Lighthouse Digest give 1869; the Lighthouse Directory gives station established 1873.
Spring freshet tore the tower from the point; quickly replaced (LighthouseFriends).
Tower toppled again; Department of Marine raised a protective shore wall around it (LighthouseFriends).
Seventh-order lens and lamp substituted for the reflectors and lamps (Marine report 1904-05; LighthouseFriends).
Reinforced concrete tower built at a cost of $985 (LighthouseFriends); Lighthouse Digest says it replaced an earlier white square wooden tower.
Present skeleton tower (Lighthouse Directory; CCG list triangular skeleton tower).

keepers.name: Michael J. Cox
keepers.note: First keeper. Owner of the land around the light; salary $80 a year (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: Micah Y. Cox
keepers.note: Second keeper; served until his death in 1892 (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: Eliza J. Cox
keepers.note: Widow of Micah Y. Cox. Placed in temporary charge of the light, with a gratuity of two months' salary (LighthouseFriends). Her appointment was cancelled after she remarried later in 1897. Her new husband was Alexander McBaine.

keepers.name: William Barton
keepers.note: Recommended by Walter Butler in 1897. Installed after a January 1898 dispute over the light; resigned by letter of 5 April 1898 on condition that McBaine be made keeper (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: George Alexander McBaine
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends: 'at least 1923'; kept the light for at least twenty years. Also spelled Alexander McBaine in LighthouseFriends' narrative. The Marine keepers' table for 1904-05 gives 'McBaine, Alex' in the Cox Point row, matched by column position (see notes_for_editor). Later Marine tables give 'McBain, Alexander'; station match not checked.

notes_for_editor: First light is unresolved: LighthouseFriends narrative 3 May 1871; LighthouseFriends data table, Lighthouse Digest and the Fredericton page 1869; Lighthouse Directory and the record (from Rowlett) 1873. The record's first_lit 1873 is left unchanged; the 1871 in facts is LighthouseFriends' narrative. Matched by position, not by printed link: the 1904-05 keepers' table (fiscal year 1904-05, scan p. 341 of the 1906 volume): McBaine, Alex and the Cox Point, Grand Lake row. The name lists and station lists are separate blocks on the scan; order matches Cox Point between Lower Neguac and Musquash Island, with MacDonald R. P. to Musquash and McMann Robert Harvey to McMann Point. The page image (Internet Archive viewer, scan p. 341) was viewed on 2026-10-28: the highlighted 'McBaine, Alex' sits in the names column in the row beside 'Cox Point, Grand Lake', with MacDonald R. P. beside Musquash Island and McMann Robert Harvey beside McMann Point. The appointment-date column is not legible at that scan resolution, so the match rests on alignment alone. The table's appointment-date column may also read as 1898 for that row, which would fit LighthouseFriends; this is not used. The 1917 concrete tower rests on LighthouseFriends, Lighthouse Digest and the Rowlett photo caption. The Marine changes-and-improvements lists for 1914 to 1917 include Cox point but their columns cannot be matched reliably, so they are not used. The 1888 and 1889 freshet damage rests only on LighthouseFriends; the corpus Marine reports start in 1900. Record items to check, not corrected: visit.boat_only is true in the record, but LighthouseFriends, Rowlett and the Fredericton page all describe a road route to the point; the record's structure height of 3.6 m differs from 3.5 m (LighthouseFriends, Fredericton) and 7.5 m (Rowlett). The Ryder bibliography on the PANB page (A few old memories: Cumberland Bay-Cox's Point, 1996) was not read. Walter Butler's 1897 letter and the 1898 correspondence are known only through LighthouseFriends' quotations; the original letters were not reached. LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: the story paraphrases it and quotes no more than a short phrase.
